title: Broad trade patterns

blocks.heading: Broad trade patterns
blocks.text: Developing, newly industrialised and developed economies participate in varied commodity, manufactured and service trade. Broad patterns can include primary-product dependence or expanding manufactures, but countries differ and also trade within these groups. A category is not a current trade-data table.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Developing economies
blocks.text: Some developing economies rely heavily on a few primary exports and imported equipment or goods. That concentration can expose receipts to price changes; it does not describe every developing country or prevent manufactured and service exports.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: NIC patterns
blocks.text: Industrial expansion can increase manufactured exports and imports of equipment or components. Participation in production chains may create jobs, while imported-input dependence and low local retention can limit gains. NIC is a broad syllabus category, not a permanent current list.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Developed economies
blocks.text: Many developed economies trade manufactures, services, technology and raw materials across extensive networks. They also differ in resources and specialisation. Higher income does not mean an economy exports every advanced product or avoids dependence.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Use the evidence
blocks.text: Describe this original fictional trade pattern: A earns 80% from primary and 20% manufactured exports; B earns 30% and 70%. A is more primary-dependent while B is more manufacture-focused: their primary shares differ by 50 percentage points, with the reverse manufactured difference. This shows composition, not total receipts or welfare.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Connect the ideas
blocks.text: Connect to Industrialisation (4.1), Production (3.1) and investment/aid (9.2). Keep transaction type, time period, units and local development criteria explicit. The data is fictional.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
